title: What is known about 1RB1LE_1LC1RE_1LE1LD_1LC0LA_1RF0LA_---0RA
description: Proof status of the six-state BB(6) holdout 1RB1LE_1LC1RE_1LE1LD_1LC0LA_1RF0LA_---0RA.
intro: Nobody knows whether this six-state, two-symbol Turing machine halts when started on a blank tape: it is one of the holdouts left open by the bbchallenge project. This page lists what has been established about it, sorted by what each result rests on.
verdict: The question is open. The head sweeps over the period-6 word 111110, which appears in all six rotations, and the leftward sweep over each rotation is a proved shift rule. Five or six walls between rotations split the tape into domains; between consecutive visits of the right end the domain lengths change by amounts in ratio 4 and the width grows by 1024. This looks like a counter in base 4, but its rule has not been written. Lean proves no halt in the first 10,000 steps by the kernel alone and in the first 107 with native_decide, and proves the shift rules of the sweeps (lean/Rules.lean); the C simulator finds no halt in the first 109 steps.

claims.title: The halting configurations
claims.text: The machine stops exactly when it reads the symbol of a halting transition (F0); the generated statement covers every configuration.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10,000 steps
claims.text: The list simulator of the shared library, proved to agree with the machine's semantics, runs 10,000 steps from blank tape without a halt, evaluated by Lean's kernel.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps
claims.text: The same run, evaluated by compiled code.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>9</sup> steps
claims.text: The C simulator tools/c/triage.c runs 109 steps without a halt; at the end 99,661 cells have been visited and 67,922 of them hold a 1.

claims.title: No halt in the first 7.19×10<sup>18</sup> steps (exact macro run)
claims.text: A macro simulator (blocks of 6 cells, long runs of equal blocks crossed in one go; exact: every macro step is a run of the machine, counted step for step) ran from blank tape to step 7,191,166,652,716,873,648 without a halt. At this block size it gives the same state, head position and tape as the direct simulator after 2,000,036,035 steps. This is a bounded run and says nothing about later steps.

claims.title: Growth shape: power/sqrt
claims.text: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.508). Right of the start it grows like a power of the step count other than 1/2 (fitted exponent 0.142).

claims.title: Shift rules of the sweeps
claims.text: The leftward sweep over the background in the four rotations it is entered in: L (111110)^n E>1 R, L (111101)^n A>1 R, L (101111)^n D>1 R and L (011111)^n C>1 R, each copy becoming a rotation of 101011, for every n and all tapes L, R.

claims.title: Domains changing in ratio 4
claims.text: The right end is visited rarely (325 times in 2·10<sup>9</sup> steps). Between consecutive visits late in the run the width grows by 1024, the first domain by 1536, and the other domains change by −384, −96, −24, −6 (each a quarter of the one before). Domain lengths are often powers of 2 or sums of few (4096, 1792, 448, 256, 872). Read off the run; not proved.

claims.title: Does it halt from blank tape?
claims.text: Not known. The machine halts on F0, reached as E>0 0 (E reads 0, moves right onto a 0). The background has no two 0s in a row, so this needs a wall of an unusual kind; whether the ratio-4 counter ever produces one is open.

check: python3 holdouts/1RB1LE_1LC1RE_1LE1LD_1LC0LA_1RF0LA_---0RA/py/rules.py | diff - holdouts/1RB1LE_1LC1RE_1LE1LD_1LC0LA_1RF0LA_---0RA/lean/Rules.lean   # the rules file is current

explainer.lede: Nobody knows. The tape is the six cells 111110 repeated, in a few stretches whose phases differ. Between visits of the head to the right end the stretches change by amounts that shrink by a factor of 4 each, like the digits of a base-4 counter. The rule has not been written.

facts.text: No halt in the C simulator; 99,661 cells visited.
No halt, proved in Lean; the first 10,000 by the kernel alone.
The growth shape of the two sides of the tape (see below).
Ratio of the changes of consecutive domains between visits of the right end.

sections.heading: One word in six rotations
html: The tape repeats 111110, but in different rotations in different domains; the walls between domains are phase shifts. The leftward sweeps are proved shift rules (lean/Rules.lean). Two end turns at step 3.7·108:

sections.heading: Changes in ratio 4
html: The head reaches the right end rarely (325 times in the first 2·109 steps). Between two such visits late in the run the width grows by 1024 cells, the first domain grows by 1536, and the next domains change by −384, −96, −24, −6: each change a quarter of the one before. With domain lengths like 4096 and 1792 that suggests a counter in base 4 whose digits are the domains. The rule has not been extracted.

sections.heading: Two 0s
html: F0 is the only halting transition, reached as E>0 0. The background never has two 0s in a row; the ends of the tape do (1100 at the right end above), so the question is whether the counter ever brings E there in the wrong phase. Open.

sections.heading: The shape of the run
html: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.508). Right of the start it grows like a power of the step count other than 1/2 (fitted exponent 0.142).
After 109 steps the tape spans 99,661 cells (69,823 left of the start, 105 right), with a density of 1s of 0.682.
These are measurements of one bounded run, sorted by tools/py/bbtools/triage.py; the macro structure behind them is the next thing to find.

summary: A bouncer over the period-6 background 111110 in all its rotations; five or six walls (phase shifts) split it into domains whose lengths change between visits of the right end by amounts in ratio 4 (−384, −96, −24, −6), with powers of 2 throughout: a counter-like structure not yet written as a rule.
family: period-6 bouncer with walls, ratio-4 hierarchy
